attribution.note: Marcus's own sentence in his own Substack post.

semantics.note: The proposition matches the sentence: three distinct tasks, with maintenance 'even harder'. One leftover inconsistency: the target field still says GenAI-written code even though the revision dropped that scope. The sentence is about coding in general.

contract.note: The plain reading is ordinary and fair: maintenance is a distinct and harder or costlier burden in software engineering. The contract rightly treats 'any coder with chops' as rhetoric. Using cost share as a stand-in for difficulty is a stretch the contract itself flags, but the degradation route (Lehman) covers difficulty.

evidence.note: Preprint dated before the post. It summarises the classic literature: maintenance is 60-80% of lifecycle cost (Brooks), and quality degrades as maintenance goes on (Lehman). This meets the support condition, though the figures come secondhand.
These results are about AI agents' regressions, not software engineering in general, so this is context only.

reviews.rationale: Established literature, as summarised in a pre-post preprint, treats maintenance as the majority of lifecycle cost and finds that code degrades as it evolves. That meets the support condition. The packet contains no counterevidence. One limit: the cost figures come through a secondary summary, and no direct measure of 'harder' was found.

attribution.note: Marcus's own closing sentence in his post.

semantics.note: 'We are going to need' is firm, so this is a scored forecast. The 'may well' clause about AI writing most code is hedged and works as a concession, not an antecedent. The forecast holds either way, and the horizon 'for a long time to come' is kept.

contract.note: Treating this as an open-horizon forecast is fair. The early-contradiction rule (routine maintenance at industry scale with no humans) is a reasonable reading of the statement. Support correctly has to wait for a long time to pass.

evidence.note: EASE 2026 study, mid-2026: humans did about 83% of maintenance on AI-generated files. This is consistent with the forecast so far and does not trigger early contradiction, but it cannot settle a 'long time to come' claim.
Early-2026 baseline: agents often cause regressions in long-term maintenance. It does not show the outcome.

reviews.rationale: This is an open-horizon forecast with no deadline. As of the evaluation date, the evidence shows humans still do most repair of AI code, so the early-contradiction rule is not met. Support needs many years to pass, so the outcome is unresolved.
